title: Intersection with an effective Cartier divisor
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subscheme of dimension $d\ge 1$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal L_1,\ldots,\mathcal L_d$ be invertible $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $D\hookrightarrow Z$ be a nonempty effective Cartier divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] with $\mathcal L_1|_Z \cong \mathcal O_Z(D)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]; this isomorphism holds in particular when $D=Z(s)$ is the zero scheme [def-pc-zero-scheme] of a section $s\in\Gamma(Z,\mathcal L_1|_Z)$ and $Z(s)$ is an effective Cartier divisor. Assume that $\dim D=d-1$ or that $Z$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Then: (a) $D$ is proper over $k$ and $\dim D=d-1$; (b) for every ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$ [def-sc-ample], the restriction $\mathcal M|_D$ is ample on $D$ in the sense of [def-sc-ample]; (c) $(\mathcal L_1\cdots\mathcal L_d\cdot Z)=(\mathcal L_2\cdots\mathcal L_d\cdot D)$, with intersection numbers defined by [def-sc-intersection-number].

source.place: Tag 0BEU (varieties intersection with an effective Cartier divisor), used in the proof of Tag 0BEV

proof.text: Replace X by Z and restrict all invertible modules. If $D=Z(s)$ for a section $s$ of $\mathcal L_1|_Z$ whose zero scheme is effective Cartier, the last sentence of [lem-pc-zero-scheme-divisor-iso] applied on $Z$ gives $\mathcal L_1|_Z\cong\mathcal O_Z(D)$. The closed immersion D\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X and properness of X over k give that D is proper over k by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. If I_D is the ideal of D, then D effective Cartier gives I_D invertible and the exact sequence 0 \to I_D \to \mathcal O_Z \to \mathcal O_D \to 0. Tensoring by an invertible module is exact because it is locally tensoring with a free rank-one module; using \mathcal L_1|_Z \cong I_D^\vee gives the Euler-characteristic difference formula.

Dimension of $D$. If $\dim D=d-1$ is assumed there is nothing to do. Otherwise $Z$ is integral; $Z$ is proper over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](c), hence of finite type over $k$ by [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $\dim Z=d\ge1$. So [lem-sc-effective-cartier-dimension-drop], applied to the integral finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ and the nonempty effective Cartier divisor $D\hookrightarrow Z$, gives $\dim D=d-1$. With the preceding step this proves (a).

source.place: Tag 0BEV proof: Z(s) effective Cartier on the variety X, hence of codimension 1 and dimension d-1

proof.text: Euler-characteristic additivity and the numerical-polynomial bound for coherent twists show that the quotient term supported on D has total degree at most d-1: its support is D, so dim Supp(O_D)=dim D=d-1 by (a), and [lem-sc-snapper-numerical-polynomial] applies. Thus the coefficient of n_1\cdots n_d in the first difference equals the coefficient of n_2\cdots n_d on D. By the definition of intersection numbers this is (L_1\cdots L_d\cdot Z)=(L_2\cdots L_d\cdot D). This proves (c).

Ampleness of $\mathcal M|_D$. By [def-sc-ample] choose $m\ge1$ with $\mathcal M^{\otimes m}$ very ample, giving a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ with $i^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal M^{\otimes m}$. The composite $D\hookrightarrow Z\hookrightarrow X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ is a closed immersion (composites of homeomorphisms onto closed subsets are such, and composites of surjections of structure sheaves are surjective, [def-weil-closed-immersion]), and it pulls $\mathcal O(1)$ back to $\mathcal M^{\otimes m}|_D$, which is therefore ample by [lem-pc-very-ample-ample]. Since $D$ is proper over $k$ by (a), [def-sc-ample] gives $m'\ge1$ with $(\mathcal M|_D)^{\otimes mm'}$ very ample, so $\mathcal M|_D$ is ample. This proves (b); the same argument is used in the proof of Tag 0BEV.
